title: Success Envelope DTO
description: Canonical success-response envelope {success, message, data} returned by backend routes that use response_handler.success_response or response_handler.paginated_response. The discriminator `success` is true (error_envelope_schema sets it false). `data` is the route-specific payload. Companion to error_envelope_schema.json. PAGINATION IS NESTED, NOT TOP-LEVEL: the canonical `paginated_response` helper is strict nested-only and emits `data.pagination` alongside `data.items` (TraigentBackend src/utils/response_handler.py:288-296 states the rule, :349-356 emits it). This schema previously declared a top-level `pagination` property, which no producer of this envelope emits; the declaration has been removed and each paginated response schema declares `pagination` inside its own `data` object. `additionalProperties` stays true, so a route that still puts pagination at the top level is not rejected by this envelope — it is simply not described by it. The authoritative backend wrap-map (which route files wrap vs return bare) is recorded in x-wrap-map so consumers and the bare/enveloped read-path can be reconciled (#136); route files that are neither wholly wrapped nor wholly bare are recorded under x-wrap-map.mixed with their enveloped operations enumerated.
x-content-note: INV-GAP (reclassified by review): open payload root accepts extra properties that carry no class; names and values are unclassified

mixed.$comment: Route files that are neither wholly wrapped nor wholly bare. A two-list bare/wrapped map cannot express this, and leaving such a file in either list states something false about most of its operations, so the exceptions are enumerated per operation instead. `default` is what the file's UNLISTED operations do; `enveloped_operations` are the ones that emit this envelope. Per-operation x-wrap-status annotations in the endpoint catalogs are the same fact at the route level.

example_set_routes.reason: TraigentBackend#3353 moved these two list reads onto response_handler.paginated_response, so they now emit {success, message, data: {items, pagination}}. The file's other operations were not migrated and still return bare jsonify bodies — including the 404/500 branches of the two migrated reads themselves (src/routes/example_set_routes.py:154-156, 335-336, 359-361), which are bare {error} / {success,error} shapes and not error_envelope_schema.json. Classifying the file wholesale as `wrapped` would be as wrong as the `bare` it replaced.

success.description: Discriminator. Always true for success responses.

message.x-content-note: INV-GAP: was closed_enum; contract has no enum/const, so the value is not provably content-free

data.x-content-note: INV-GAP S1,S3,S5,O2,H1: not inventoried (free object/array): data
